articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 27, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 27, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, July 27, 2026.
Skyroot put India’s spacetech industry on the main orbit though next five years will prove crucial, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured news
India has cracked rocket science. Now comes the hard part: Rocket Economics
Skyroot's success isn't the climax of India's space story but the start of its commercial phase. The next 5 years belong to whoever builds the market.
Shalini Neelankavil of Honeywell PSS on women, AI, and leadership
Shalini Neelankavil, CTO of Honeywell Productivity Solutions & Services, shares how career breaks, mentorship, flexible work, and sponsorship helped shape her journey, and why women need stronger support in tech.
This startup helps brands get discovered across AI search platforms
As AI begins to reshape how people discover products and services online, Gurugram-based DareAISearch is building tools to help brands stay visible across platforms such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity.
Funding news
Nuvola Spirits raises Rs 2.69 Cr from United Spirits
Premium liqueurs startup Nuvola Spirits has raised Rs 2.69 crore from United Spirits Ltd. (USL), which will acquire a 10.08% stake in the company. The investment will support Nuvola Spirits' expansion, strengthen its distribution network and accelerate the launch of premium international spirits in India.
Founded in 2023 by Aakriti Kochhar Sachdeva and Raghav Sachdeva, the company markets Mikiamo Italian Liqueurs and Seoulmate, a Korean-inspired soju brand. Nuvola aims to build a portfolio of globally inspired premium spirits tailored for Indian consumers while making high-quality products more accessible. The partnership with USL is expected to enhance the company's market reach as premium alcohol consumption continues to grow in India.
90+ My Tuition App secures investment from Equity Intelligence
Bengaluru-based edtech company 90+ My Tuition App has received a strategic investment from Equity Intelligence, led by investor Porinju Veliyath. The funding will be used to expand the company's CBSE tuition programmes across India and develop its AI Teacher Programme to deliver personalised learning experiences.
Founded in 2018 by Vingish Vijay, the platform offers live online tuition for CBSE and Kerala State syllabus students and has supported over five lakh learners across India and GCC countries. The company also plans to strengthen its technology infrastructure, product innovation and academic operations, aiming to widen its national footprint as demand for AI-powered education solutions continues to rise.
Other news
OnGrid launches consumer background verification platform
Digital trust and background verification company OnGrid has launched Veriffy, a direct-to-consumer platform that enables individuals to conduct background checks for personal use. Built on OnGrid's enterprise verification infrastructure, Veriffy allows users to verify domestic helpers, tenants, matrimonial prospects and small business staff after obtaining their consent.
Verification requests can be completed digitally in under five minutes, with password-protected reports delivered within 24 hours through email and WhatsApp. The platform offers identity, address, employment, credit and court record checks while complying with data privacy regulations. OnGrid said it plans to add official police verification in the next phase as it expands into the consumer safety segment.
Piramal Finance, Muthoot Fincorp partner for co-lending
Piramal Finance Ltd. has partnered with Muthoot Fincorp Ltd. under a co-lending arrangement to improve access to affordable housing finance and MSME loan-against-property products across India. The partnership combines Piramal Finance's lending capabilities with Muthoot Fincorp's customer reach to extend formal credit to aspiring homeowners, self-employed professionals and small business owners.
The companies will primarily target customers in Tier II and Tier III cities, semi-urban areas and rural markets. The collaboration aims to simplify the borrowing process while expanding financial inclusion by making housing and business loans more accessible to underserved borrowers across Bharat.
Earntra crosses Rs 200 Cr loan disbursals
Earntra, the B2B Direct Selling Agent (DSA) platform operated by MyMoneyMantra.com, has facilitated cumulative loan disbursals exceeding Rs 200 crore through its network of over one lakh partners across more than 750 cities. The platform offers access to products including personal loans, home loans, business loans, loans against property and credit cards.
Earntra enables individuals to become authorised DSAs through a fully digital onboarding process supported by online training, real-time application tracking and automated commission payouts. The company said the platform is helping formalise India's traditionally fragmented financial distribution ecosystem and is well positioned to tap rising demand for retail credit, particularly across Tier II, III and IV markets.
Tredence launches Forward Deployed Engineering practice
Data and AI services firm Tredence has launched a new Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) practice and plans to build a team of 200 specialists over the next 12 to 18 months. The initiative aims to help Fortune 100 enterprises accelerate AI adoption by combining deep domain expertise with engineering capabilities. Tredence said its FDEs will specialise in sectors such as retail, supply chain and revenue growth management while developing agentic AI systems tailored to business needs.
The engineers will work across technology platforms including Databricks, Google Cloud, Microsoft, Snowflake and AWS, enabling clients to modernise enterprise data infrastructure and scale AI-driven decision-making.
JIIF appoints Anshu Jain as Chief Operating Officer
Early-stage investment platform JITO Incubation and Innovation Foundation (JIIF) has appointed Anshu Jain as its Chief Operating Officer to strengthen its leadership team and expand its national innovation ecosystem.
Jain has been associated with JIIF's incubation initiatives, strategic partnerships and startup collaborations. In her new role, she will lead the organisation's operational strategy, expand its national footprint and drive programmes supporting entrepreneurs and early-stage ventures.
With experience in startup incubation, innovation strategy and institutional partnerships, she has worked closely with investors, corporates, academic institutions and government bodies. JIIF said the appointment reinforces its commitment to building a stronger innovation ecosystem and accelerating the growth of startups across multiple sectors.
NYVO launches affordable financial planning platform
SEBI-registered investment adviser NYVO has launched a digital financial planning platform aimed at making professional wealth management accessible to Indian households. The fee-only platform integrates investments, insurance and financial goals into a personalised plan while allowing users to connect existing mutual fund portfolios and receive goal-based recommendations.
NYVO said the service is available for less than Rs 100 a month, removing minimum investment barriers and making financial advice accessible regardless of portfolio size. The platform uses an in-house asset allocation model and mutual fund rating engine that evaluates market trends and fund quality rather than relying solely on historical performance. The company aims to simplify long-term financial planning for Indian families.
Neo Group appoints Anirban Banerjee as Co-founder
Wealth and asset management firm Neo Group has appointed Anirban Banerjee as Co-founder and Chief People and Transformation Officer to strengthen its leadership team as it expands its operations. Banerjee will lead the company's people strategy, talent development, leadership capability, organisational design and enterprise transformation initiatives.
He joins Neo after serving as Chief Human Resources Officer at Avendus Group and was previously part of the leadership team at 360 ONE. Neo currently manages around Rs 1.3 lakh crore in client assets across wealth and asset management businesses and serves family offices, high-net-worth individuals, institutions and corporates through a network of more than 30 locations with a workforce of approximately 850 professionals.
Electromech Infraprojects partners Nova Capital for UAE data centres
Electromech Infraprojects Ltd. has signed a memorandum of understanding with Nova Capital Enterprises, a subsidiary of Abu Dhabi-based Al Nasser Holdings, to jointly pursue data centre projects across the UAE and the wider Middle East.
The partnership combines Electromech's expertise in mission-critical engineering and digital infrastructure with Al Nasser Holdings' regional presence to develop hyperscale data centres and other advanced digital infrastructure projects.
The collaboration aligns with the UAE's ambitions to expand its artificial intelligence, sovereign cloud and digital economy capabilities. The companies expect rising investments in AI and cloud computing to drive demand for resilient, sustainable and future-ready data centre infrastructure across the GCC region.
Dreamfly to set up aviation battery manufacturing facility in Bengaluru
Indian deep-tech company Dreamfly Innovations has announced plans to establish a 40,000 sq. ft. aviation battery manufacturing facility in North Bengaluru to support India's growing drone industry. The facility will have an initial annual production capacity of 100 MWh, scalable to 200 MWh, making it one of the country's largest aviation battery plants dedicated to drones.
The batteries will cater to defence, surveillance, agriculture, logistics and emerging air mobility applications, including air taxis. Dreamfly said the project will strengthen domestic manufacturing of critical drone components, reduce dependence on imports and support the government's push for indigenous drone production under initiatives such as the Kisan Drone Policy.
ePlane Company signs strategic partnerships for eVTOL ecosystem
The ePlane Company, an Indian developer of electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, has announced a series of strategic partnerships at the Farnborough International Airshow 2026 to strengthen the supply chain for its e200X platform. The collaborations span advanced materials, avionics, medical interiors and other critical systems, reinforcing the company's Make in India manufacturing ecosystem as it advances towards aircraft certification.
Founder and CTO Prof. Satya Chakravarthy said the partnerships strengthen the company's journey towards building a certifiable, Made-in-India electric aircraft. The agreements are expected to enhance the development of the e200X platform while expanding the trusted industrial ecosystem supporting India's emerging electric aviation sector and future advanced air mobility solutions.
Pegasystems expands university programme in India
Enterprise AI software company Pegasystems has expanded its University Academic Program (UAP) in India by onboarding implementation partners ai4process, The Skill Enhancers and Tinkr Learning alongside existing partner SmartBridge Educational Services.
The initiative aims to build a larger pipeline of industry-ready talent as demand grows for professionals skilled in AI and intelligent automation. Scheduled to begin in August 2026, the programme will initially train over 500 engineering students before scaling to between 800 and 1,000 students across more than 50 university campuses. The curriculum combines hands-on training in Pega's AI technologies with industry-relevant consulting skills, certification opportunities and faculty development to improve graduates' employability in enterprise AI and automation.
Salesforce partners Vivekananda Hospital for AI-powered patient engagement
Salesforce has partnered with Vivekananda Hospital Pvt. Ltd. (VHPL) in West Bengal to modernise patient engagement using its AI-powered Agentforce 360 Platform. Integrated with the hospital's information management system, the platform provides unified Patient 360 and Doctor 360 views while enabling automated enquiry management, campaign tracking and real-time dashboards.
The digital solution also supports QR code-based community outreach campaigns, helping hospital teams capture and manage patient enquiries efficiently. During VHPL's Mega Health Carnival in January 2026, the platform processed over 600 patient enquiries in three days. Salesforce said the collaboration will improve patient engagement, streamline workflows and enable healthcare teams to deliver faster and more personalised services.
Wipro strengthens AI partnership with Databricks
Wipro has expanded its partnership with Databricks to help enterprises modernise data infrastructure and accelerate large-scale AI adoption. As part of the collaboration, Wipro has established a dedicated Databricks business practice focused on developing industry-specific AI solutions and accelerators. The partnership combines Databricks' capabilities in agentic AI, data modernisation and analytics with Wipro Intelligence and the WEGA agent-native delivery platform.
The initiative aims to help organisations transition from fragmented data environments and pilot AI projects to enterprise-scale AI deployments. The companies said the enhanced collaboration will enable businesses to modernise legacy systems, optimise existing data investments and build scalable, AI-ready data architectures across industries.
UPES, HPE launch AI-driven networking centre
UPES has partnered with Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) to establish the HPE Networking AI-Driven Centre of Excellence, aimed at preparing students for careers in AI-powered networking, cloud computing and cybersecurity. The centre will integrate industry-led curriculum, faculty development, hands-on laboratory training, certification programmes, bootcamps and research opportunities into the university's academic framework.
Students will also gain access to HPE Networking certifications, internships and potential hiring opportunities through HPE and its partner ecosystem. UPES said the initiative reflects its AI-first education strategy by embedding artificial intelligence across disciplines rather than limiting it to computer science, helping graduates develop skills required for the evolving enterprise technology workforce.
DeepFacts charts India expansion for AI healthcare platform
HealthTech startup DeepFacts Pvt. Ltd., creator of the AI-enabled remote patient monitoring platform proRITHM, has announced plans to expand across Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Odisha before entering markets across India by early 2027. The company, which already has a strong presence in Telangana, also plans to enter the US market by late 2027 or early 2028.
DeepFacts combines wearable technology with artificial intelligence to enable continuous patient monitoring and early health risk detection. The company has secured three patents for its proprietary technologies and aims to improve healthcare accessibility through AI-powered remote monitoring while strengthening collaborations with healthcare providers across domestic and international markets.
Eco Kranti summit selects over 30 sustainability startups
The inaugural Eco Kranti Shubh Labh 1.0 National Summit has selected more than 30 startups focused on sustainability and social innovation. Organised by Eco Kranti, an initiative of the Sri Sri Rural Development Programme, in collaboration with Startup India and DPIIT, the summit brought together entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and researchers to promote climate-positive innovations.
The event focused on sectors including climate technology, waste management, circular economy, green manufacturing and rural innovation. Eco Kranti said its movement has already reached over 10,000 households and helped prevent nearly 200 tonnes of single-use plastic waste. It now aims to reach 10 lakh households and prevent 1,000 tonnes of plastic waste over the next two years.
Bhanzu launches nationwide Math Bee championship
Edtech platform Bhanzu has partnered with NODWIN Gaming and Rusk Media to launch Math Bee, a reality show-style mathematics championship for students in Classes 7 to 9. The competition combines academic excellence with entertainment, featuring celebrity hosts and judges in an OTT-format series.
Students will qualify through Bhanzu's MathUp app before progressing to virtual bootcamps and the televised finals, where India's first Math Bee champion will be crowned. Unlike conventional examinations, the competition rewards logical thinking, creativity, speed and problem-solving. Bhanzu said the initiative aims to reduce mathematics anxiety and inspire students to embrace the subject through engaging, technology-driven learning experiences that make mathematics more aspirational.
The Foundery showcases 18 consumer startups
The Foundery, the venture builder co-founded by Kishore Biyani, Nikhil Kamath and Ronnie Screwvala, has unveiled 18 consumer brands at its inaugural investor showcase, The Foundery FWD. Developed through the venture builder's 90-day residential programme, the startups span health and wellness, beauty, fashion, food and beverage, lifestyle and consumer technology.
The brands will now enter the market through Broadway's experiential retail stores, allowing founders to test customer demand, study buying behaviour and refine products before scaling. The initiative offers startups temporary shelf space through a cost-effective commercial model, enabling them to validate products without investing in permanent retail infrastructure. The programme aims to accelerate the growth of early-stage consumer businesses in India.
BitDelta India launches crypto assets learning and certification programme
BitDelta India, an FIU-IND-registered Virtual Digital Asset trading platform has announced the launch of CrypTution, an institution grade crypto assets (VDA) learning and certification ecosystem. CrypTution has been developed with an aim to support the growth of India’s VDA ecosystem through informed and prepared participation.
While access to crypto assets and related information has expanded, formal education has not kept pace, leaving many participants to navigate a complex and evolving market through fragmented sources, a statement noted.
The initiative aims to bridge this gap by combining guided learning, simulated market exposure and competency-led certification before participants transition to live-market environments. With Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities already accounting for nearly 40% of India's crypto user base, the initiative is designed to make structured VDA education more accessible across geographies, languages and participant profiles.

articles.title: These are the 3 Batman 4K Blu-rays I'll be watching at home as I wait for The Batman Part II — and one of them is sure to be a controversial pick
articles.text:
The Batman Part II has been delayed again, so I'll have to stick with 4K Blu-ray at home for now — here are 3 Batman discs I recommend, including a controversial choice
3 of my favorite of the Caped Crusader's adventures
As a Batman fan, I was disappointed to learn last week that The Batman Part 2 has been delayed until February 18, 2028, another four-month wait to add to add to its last (delayed) intended release date of October 1, 2027. This latest holdup is actually the fourth time the long-awaited sequel to The Batman has been delayed, with its initial release originally set to be October 2025.
Thankfully, there are plenty of ways to enjoy Batman content at home while we eagerly await The Batman: Part 2’s 2028 release. From Christopher Nolan’s iconic Dark Knight Trilogy to the awesome Batman: The Animated Series, there are tons of choices. And there’s no better way to enjoy Batman’s many adventures than with a 4K Blu-ray. I’m a 4K Blu-ray fan and collector, so I’m always testing the latest releases for the Blu-ray Bounty and finding new discs to test the best TVs and best soundbars.
Below, I’ve picked three of my favorite Batman-related 4K Blu-rays, not just because they’re my personal picks, but because they’re also great examples to show what 4K can do, especially for your home theater.
The Batman
Where else to better prepare for The Batman: Part 2 than with its predecessor, The Batman. Matt Reeve’s The Batman follows Bruce Wayne (Robert Pattison) in his second year as Batman, where he must face The Riddler (Paul Dano), a revolutionary who uses a series of riddles and puzzles to test Batman, as Riddler plans to expose Gotham’s corrupt government and elite.
The Batman has become one of my main 4K Blu-rays for testing TVs. Due to its low brightness, some TVs can really struggle to accurately display the movie, compromising its dark tones. But, there’s also plenty of excellent-looking scenes with powerful contrast, balancing light and dark tones, that can really show off a TV.
The opening 20 minutes of the movie itself is all a big demo-reel for contrast. From the dark subway platform illuminated by overhead lamps as Batman fights a gang of thugs, to where we first see Bruce decoding Riddler’s clues in the Batcave, The Batman delivers truly dynamic and strong contrast, which I've found look superb on the best OLED TVs in particular.
There’s also a chance to show a display’s shadow detail, with plenty of scenes making use of shadows to create a captivating image. The aforementioned subway scene is one of these, with truly dark shadows creating a foreboding atmosphere that fits the gloomy tone of the movie.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There’s excellent detail throughout, with crisp textures that look refined and lifelike. Close-up shots show scars, wrinkles and stubble on people’s faces with impressive clarity, and texture in environments, like Mayor Mitchell’s house or the Batcave, are given a near-3D level of detail.
The Batman is an audio showcase as well as a visual one. The Batmobile chase has become a reference scene I use for showing off a sound system. The ignition of the Batmobile’s engines deliver room-rattling, powerful bass that through a subwoofer can create some serious roar. The 4K disc uses a Dolby Atmos soundtrack that creates an immersive and detailed sound.
As the Batmobile chases Penguin across a busy freeway, serving traffic and blaring horns are accurately mapped to the action. As Penguin fires a spray of bullets at the Batmobile, the sound glides around a surround system, as I found when using soundbars such as the talented Samsung HW-Q990H. There are plenty of Atmos effects too, as rain regularly falls throughout the movie, effectively using the height channels of any sound system.
The Dark Knight
Arguably the most popular Batman movie ever made, The Dark Knight is the second movie in Christopher Nolan’s trilogy. It’s one that’s stuck with me ever since I saw it as a teenager in theaters in 2008. Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) is a couple of years into his time as Batman and he faces his biggest challenge yet, when he squares off with the unpredictable and chaotic Joker (played brilliantly by Heath Ledger).
Unsurprisingly, where this disc shines is in its IMAX sequences. These IMAX scenes show impeccable detail and crisp, 3D-like textures. In the opening bank heist scene, every detail is refined, from the creases in the robbers’ masks, to the texture in buildings of the densely packed city. Oh, and don’t be surprised when the ratio changes from widescreen to fullscreen: that’s normal for IMAX on home media.
Black tones and shadow detail are excellent during the film's night scenes too (of which there are plenty), and they look superb on an OLED TV. Contrast is also strong, particularly during the prison escort scene. As trucks move under the freeway, the overhead lights balance well with the dark, shadowed areas of the tunnel to create dynamic contrast.
This disc is also an audio powerhouse. With a DTS-HD 5.1 MA soundtrack, there’s some fantastic detail. During the tunnel escort scene, the whir of Batman’s bike riding through the tunnel is mapped perfectly to every channel. As perspective changes, so does the sound. Bullets are precise, flying from the front to rear channels when the movie is from Batman’s point-of-view, and every individual effect is audible, such as flying debris and swerving tyres.
Bass throughout the movie is truly powerful. Bullets have serious impact and the roar of the Batmobile’s engines delivers tightly controlled, but hefty low-end that reverberated through our testing room when I watched.
The score is a showcase in and of itself, with superb separation across different channels of the Samsung HW-Q990C soundbar I was using. In the opening scene, the scratching strings came from the left rear, the ticking sound from the right, and the heavy bass exploded from the subwoofer. Crucially though, every element was perfectly balanced, within the score itself and with all the action.
Batman Forever
This pick will raise eyebrows, I’m sure. But, honestly, Batman Forever is the Batman movie I grew up with and despite its very corny nature, I enjoy it. It scratches the exact part of my brain that occasionally craves a nostalgic Batman fix. The movie follows Batman (played by Val Kilmer) as he does battle with the Riddler (Jim Carrey) and Two-Face (Tommy Lee Jones) as they attempt to take over Gotham.
While this may be a surprising choice for a lot of people, this is a seriously good-looking 4K presentation. Batman Forever uses a lot of bold and vibrant colors, and in 4K, they really pop on screen. The green of the Riddler’s gaudy outfit and the purple of Two-Face’s injured side compliment each other well. There’s also a lot of neon-esuqe lighting used in the movie, with light tubes, red detail on Two-Face’s minion’s guns and the shimmering greens of Riddler’s hideout and event space. All these colors have a gorgeous punch that looks sharp and dynamic throughout the movie.
Shadows are used a lot, with characters often standing over lamps or in shaded rooms to create strong contrast in images. The LG G6 OLED on which I watched this movie in our testing room celebrates these rich and inky dark tones, with the leather of Batman’s armor showing nice depth, but also balancing well as the light reflects off it. Shadow detail is excellent too, with textures in dark areas on screen legible (yes, even the strange texture of Batman’s armor). Skin looks realistic in the many close-up shots used, too.
This 4K disc also supports Dolby Atmos. There’s some excellent use of height channels throughout, with the sound of helicopter Two-Face uses to escape in the intro coming from overhead as I watched. Explosions have plenty of meat to them, producing some lovely low-end rumble during the movie’s more action-packed scenes. The sound of the Batmobile’s engines firing is another great demo for the powerful bass in the mix.
More subtle details are also fully audible. The sound of Batman’s batarang as he throws it is precisely mapped, with the sound eagerly following its trajectory. Bullets have great punch to them, and again these are accurately posited within the surround channels. Speech is consistently clear throughout too, even during the most chaotic scenes. You might not necessarily expect this movie to be such an audio showcase, but it really is.

La hausse serait moins avantageuse pour les Pro XL et Fold, qui gagneraient peu en équipement. Certaines versions du Pixel 11 Pro pourraient même passer de 16 à 12 Go de RAM pour réduire les coûts. Les data centers destinés à l’IA absorbent une part croissante des puces produites par Samsung, SK Hynix et d’autres fournisseurs. Un gigaoctet de RAM serait ainsi passé d’environ 2,80 $ en 2025 à 12 $ en 2026. Google prévoit donc des révisions tarifaires variables selon l’approvisionnement, y compris pour des produits déjà commercialisés. Le Pixel 10a, qui doit rester disponible jusqu’au printemps 2027, semble particulièrement exposé, tout comme potentiellement la Pixel Watch.

articles.title: Apple está preparando unas gafas para responder a las Ray-Ban de Meta. El problema es un muro llamado 'privacidad'
articles.text:
John Ternus es el nuevo CEO de Apple y, aunque asumirá el cargo oficialmente el próximo 1 de septiembre coincidiendo con la presentación de los iPhone 18 Pro, llega al cargo con tarea. Por un lado, el rumoreadísimo iPhone plegable que deberíamos ver junto a los iPhone 18 Pro y que tendría un formato muy similar a lo visto en el Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.
Por otro lado, las nuevas gafas de Apple. No nos referimos a una nueva versión de las Vision Pro, sino a un producto más de llevar en el día a día con el que entrarán a competir, directamente, contra las Ray-Ban de Meta. Sin embargo, hay un desafío importante en este producto: la privacidad.
Porque las gafas de Meta llevan tiempo surcando mares de polémicas con la privacidad, las grabaciones de usuarios que no son tan privadas o el uso que se hace de este tipo de dispositivo, y si una empresa no quiere tener nada que ver con polémicas, y menos relacionadas con privacidad, esa es Apple.
Todo ello los está obligando a pensar muy mucho qué estrategia quieren seguir con estas gafas que pueden pagar los platos rotos de otro equipo: el de IA. Vamos con la historia porque tiene bastante chicha.
Las gafas de Apple y el problema de la privacidad
Hace unos meses, nuestros compañeros de Applesfera ya contaban que fuentes reputadas tanto del sector en general como de Apple en particular apuntaban a un retraso en las gafas de Apple. Mark Gurman, en Bloomberg, asegura que el dispositivo estaba previsto para algún momento de 2026, pero al final terminará llegando a finales de 2027 con una presentación en la WWDC 2027.
Ese tiempo extra permitirá a los desarrolladores crear apps para un nuevo tipo de wearable que aspira a ser un Apple Watch, pero en forma de gafas. También dará más tiempo para que la propia compañía lidie con el asunto de la privacidad.
Recientemente hemos visto varias polémicas relacionadas con las gafas de Meta en este ámbito y, aunque Meta no ha respondido a algunas de esas polémicas, sí ha tomado medidas parcheando la manipulación de los usuarios e impidiendo que las gafas graben si detectan que el LED que funciona como 'chivato' cuando grabamos está alterado.
Según Gurman, las gafas tienen como nombre en código 'N50' y Apple ha puesto a trabajar a varios de sus equipos (ingeniería y marketing entre ellos) para refinar no sólo el producto, sino el mensaje alrededor de la privacidad del nuevo dispositivo. Es, según el periodista de Bloomberg, la principal prioridad de Apple de cara a estas gafas debido a la inquietud de los usuarios y al escrutinio público y legal al respecto.
La desconfianza ya ha llevado a que tanto estados como entidades privadas las prohíban en algunos espacios (como en piscinas, gimnasios o escuelas, por ejemplo) y, aunque los móviles capturan imágenes de más resolución y calidad, llevar una cámara en las gafas se siente más furtivo, como un dispositivo de captura más silenciosa.
Apple sabe que muchos ojos estarán puestos en este asunto cuando presente el dispositivo, por lo que está trabajando para enfatizar no sólo las áreas en las que sus gafas se diferencien del resto, sino también por qué el usuario (y la propia sociedad) puede confiar en él. La idea es que este dispositivo sea una mezcla entre AirPods y Apple Watch con acceso a Siri, reproducción de música, llamadas e información, y Gurman apunta que una solución al tema de la privacidad sería eliminar las cámaras o impedir, directamente, que el usuario pueda capturar contenido.
Unas gafas inteligentes sin cámara no es tan raro. Xiaomi tiene unas y hay marcas con productos así que, precisamente, se apoyan en esa mejora en la privacidad como arma de marketing. En Bloomberg aseguran que Apple estaría planteando unas gafas sin cámara, pero también una con cámaras y sensores, pero que sólo se usen para que la IA vea el mundo alrededor del usuario y obtenga información sobre objetos y lugares que, posteriormente, trasladaría al usuario mediante Siri.
Hay dos problemas. El primero es que, si la privacidad no fuera un problema y en un mundo ideal, unas gafas con cámara son extremadamente útiles para grabar momentos familiares y crear contenido con las manos libres, por lo que eliminar las cámaras haría que los que quieran eso se vayan a la competencia. El segundo es que Gurman afirma que Apple no confía actualmente en su IA como para que sea ese el principal argumento de venta de un producto totalmente nuevo.
Evidentemente, es un asunto espinoso y difícil de abordar para una Apple que está a punto de entrar en un periodo de celebración (con el rumoreado iPhone de 20 aniversario), pero que tiene varias patatas calientes como potenciales subidas de precio (aún más) debido a la crisis de la RAM y productos totalmente nuevos para ellos como estas gafas o el plegable. Muchas posibles crisis que afrontar si algo sale mal, por lo que es lógico que quieran ir con pies de plomo.

articles.title: AI developer runs 28.9-million-parameter model on $10 ESP32-S3 microcontroller — uses Google's Per-Layer Embeddings technique, stores table on 16MB Flash memory
articles.text:
AI developer runs 28.9-million-parameter model on $10 ESP32-S3 microcontroller — uses Google's Per-Layer Embeddings technique, stores table on 16MB Flash memory
Local model running on a sub-$10 microcontroller is impressive despite its obvious limitations.
When we talk about running local AI these days, the conversation usually either revolves around mini-PCs like the RTX Spark or drifts into wistful thinking about home servers and ludicrously expensive professional GPUs. Well, I reckon the most impressive AI hardware trick in a good while just happened on a piece of silicon that costs less than a decent burger. Last week, a Ukrainian developer named Slava S, who simply goes by 'slvDev' on GitHub, dropped a project called ESP32-AI. It's exactly what you think: he got a 28.9-million-parameter language model running locally, entirely on-device, on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller.
If you haven't read any of our previous coverage of this tiny chip, ESP32-S3 boards offer about the best bang for buck in the whole computing world. You can snag one online with a protective case for under $20 here in the States, and bare boards are readily available for under $10 around most of the world. As you'd expect from a chip so cheap, it's not powerful. On this variant, the S3, you get exactly 512KB of SRAM, 8MB of PSRAM, and 16MB of flash memory, which is not very much memory at all. So how exactly do you cram a nearly 30-million parameter model onto a chip with less primary storage than a single raw photo from your smartphone?
Usually, to run an LLM, the entire model has to sit in your system's fast memory because the processor needs to constantly do math against every parameter to generate the next word. If you try to run a 29M parameter model normally on an ESP32, you run out of fast RAM instantly. The previous record for a chip like this was around 260,000 parameters by one Mr. Dave Bennett, as pointed out by Slava himself on X.
Our clever hacker got around this bottleneck by borrowing a brilliant architectural trick from Google's Gemma called Per-Layer Embeddings. He quantized the model down to 4-bit (making the total file size just 14.9 MB) and changed where the data lives; instead of trying to stuff the whole thing into the tiny 512KB SRAM or the only slightly-less-tiny 8MB PSRAM, he dumped the 25-million-parameter embedding table into the relatively-slow 16MB Flash memory. Because this specific model architecture only needs to pull a few rows from this table per token, the inherent slowness of the Flash memory doesn't choke the processor, and so the 512KB of fast SRAM is kept clear for just the "thinking core", the actual reasoning weights.
Now, let's pump the brakes for a second, because I know someone out there is already wondering if they can replace their server with an $8 chip. The model he used was trained on the TinyStories dataset, and it's really more of a Small Language Model (SLM), or honestly, a "micro LM." Due to the way it was created, it's only capable of writing short, simple, fictional stories. It will not answer questions, it will not follow instructions, it won't write your Python code, and it possesses exactly zero factual knowledge about the real world.
Focusing on that limitation completely misses the magic of what's happening here in this proof-of-concept, though. The achievement is fitting a structurally quite large model onto a computer with practically no resources. It proves that with clever architecture, you can run genuine neural networks on dirt-cheap embedded hardware, and there are useful applications for a model this size. Slava imagines the idea of a coffee machine that actually knows about coffee: every bean, grind, ratio, water temperature, all offline, no app required.
Truthfully, when we're talking about "AI", it all comes down to what you are trying to accomplish. To put it plainly, asking how much hardware you need for local AI without specifying the workload is like asking what vehicle you need without saying what the goal is. A bicycle, a sedan, a pickup truck, a semi-trailer, and a train all "get you from A to B," but they're built for radically different jobs. AI is the exact same way; it's what you're doing with it that determines how much hardware you need.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
To illustrate the point, last year another developer published a project cramming an AI language model (a bigram name generator) into the original Dragon Warrior and Final Fantasy games on the NES. Yes, the Nintendo Entertainment System. Developer Emanuele Rodolà managed to fit the entire model weight table (729 bytes) and the inference code (~140 bytes of hand-written assembly) into the original game ROM to generate new character names on the fly. That's real AI, running on a MOS 6502 processor, a piece of silicon that dates back to 1975.
The ultimate takeaway from slvDev's project is that Per-Layer Embeddings scale far further down than most people would have imagined, and it lends credence to the recent enthusiasm surrounding High-Bandwidth Flash as a tiered storage medium for AI servers. That's exciting not because it means an ESP32 will replace your desktop GPU, but because it suggests the same architectural ideas could make AI dramatically more practical across the entire spectrum of hardware, from tiny embedded devices all the way up to datacenter accelerators.

articles.title: La fin annoncée des copies pirates de Windows 11 n’aura pas lieu, du moins pas comme vous l’imaginiez
articles.text:
Microsoft va imposer une attestation TPM aux serveurs KMS utilisés par les organisations. Une protection destinée à sécuriser l’activation en volume, pas à désactiver en bloc les copies pirates de Windows installées sur les PC personnels.
En novembre 2025, Microsoft neutralisait KMS38, méthode frauduleuse qui permettait d’activer Windows 10 et Windows 11 jusqu’en 2038. Huit mois plus tard, le 22 juillet dernier, l’entreprise présentait KMS Hardware-Secured, un dispositif conçu pour vérifier par TPM l’identité et l’intégrité des serveurs en charge de l’activation des parcs Windows. Une annonce aussitôt interprétée comme un nouveau tour de vis contre les copies pirates de l’OS, voire comme le prélude à une désactivation généralisée des PC concernés. Les précisions publiées depuis révèlent toutefois une mesure bien plus ciblée.
Une protection réservée aux serveurs KMS des entreprises
Pour rappel, KMS, pour Key Management Service, est le système utilisé par les organisations pour activer en volume les PC Windows de leur parc. L’entreprise installe un serveur KMS sur son réseau et l’authentifie auprès de Microsoft à l’aide de sa clé de licence. Les postes se tournent ensuite vers ce serveur pour obtenir leur activation, sans contacter directement Microsoft. Celle-ci reste valable 180 jours, mais Windows tente de la renouveler tous les sept jours.
Or, si elle est bien pratique pour les entreprises, cette dépendance aux serveurs KMS peut aussi être exploitée par des fraudeurs, capables de déployer de faux serveurs ou de cloner des hôtes légitimes afin d’activer des machines non couvertes par les licences de l’organisation. KMS Hardware-Secured doit donc limiter ces détournements en obligeant chaque serveur à prouver son identité matérielle grâce au TPM. La puce devra aussi attester que la plateforme n’a pas été altérée depuis son enregistrement.
La transition débutera en août 2026. Windows Server 2025 indiquera alors si le serveur est compatible avec cette protection, sans encore bloquer les activations. L’attestation TPM ne deviendra obligatoire qu’avec la prochaine version LTSC de Windows Server, dont la date de sortie n’a pas encore été communiquée.
Pas encore une arme générale contre le piratage de Windows
Lorsque l’attestation deviendra obligatoire, les entreprises devront disposer d’un serveur KMS conforme pour continuer à activer leurs postes. En cas d’échec de la vérification, les nouvelles machines ne pourront plus obtenir de licence, tandis que celles déjà activées conserveront leur statut jusqu’à l’expiration du délai de 180 jours. Sans renouvellement d’ici là, elles finiront par perdre leur activation.
Ce scénario ne s’applique cependant qu’aux postes qui dépendent réellement du serveur KMS officiel d’une organisation. Les copies pirates installées sur les PC personnels reposent généralement sur d’autres procédés, qui n’ont pas besoin de cette infrastructure.
Les outils d’activation qui imitent KMS font ainsi répondre un serveur local factice ou distant aux demandes de Windows. Comme Microsoft n’annonce aucune vérification de l’attestation TPM par le PC client, ils ne sont pas directement visés. La méthode KMS38 ne reposait même pas sur un serveur actif, puisqu’elle falsifiait localement la durée de validité de la licence. Quant aux outils qui cherchent à faire reconnaître une fausse licence numérique ou modifient directement les données d’activation, ils échappent eux aussi à la nouvelle protection.
KMS Hardware-Secured pourra donc empêcher une partie des détournements qui touchent les infrastructures d’entreprise, mais pas provoquer une désactivation généralisée des copies pirates de Windows.

articles.title: Tu próxima casa estará lista en 24 horas gracias a esta IA e la impresión 3D
articles.text:
La construcción de casas con impresión 3D e inteligencia artificial está revolucionando los métodos tradicionales del sector. Este avance tecnológico permite levantar viviendas en tan solo 24 horas, transformando los procesos de diseño, planificación y ejecución en proyectos mucho más rápidos, precisos y sostenibles.
La aparición de la impresión 3D y la inteligencia artificial en la arquitectura ha impulsado una nueva etapa para el desarrollo de viviendas. Estas herramientas digitales no solo aceleran los tiempos de obra, sino que también optimizan el uso de materiales, reducen el desperdicio y permiten adaptaciones personalizadas para cada familia.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo es la construcción de casas en 24 horas
Uno de los aspectos más llamativos de esta innovación es la velocidad de ejecución. Mientras que una vivienda tradicional requiere entre cuatro y doce meses para completarse, la estructura de una casa impresa en 3D puede estar lista en solo 24 a 72 horas.
El proceso completo, incluyendo acabados y detalles finales, según CMYK Arquitectos, suele culminar en un plazo de cinco a quince días, dependiendo del tamaño y las características del proyecto.
PUBLICIDAD
El proceso comienza con un diseño digital elaborado en software CAD (Diseño Asistido por Computadora). Este diseño se convierte en una guía para la impresora 3D, que deposita material de construcción —como hormigón, polímeros o compuestos de cemento— capa por capa, siguiendo el modelo digital. La precisión de la máquina reduce errores, minimiza el desperdicio de materiales y optimiza el tiempo de trabajo.
Durante la construcción, la inteligencia artificial juega un papel central para coordinar el proceso, detectar posibles fallos y optimizar cada fase. Algoritmos avanzados controlan el flujo de materiales, la calidad de las capas impresas y el cumplimiento de los estándares estructurales.
PUBLICIDAD
Así, se garantiza que la vivienda cumpla con todas las normativas de seguridad y durabilidad, al mismo tiempo que se personaliza según las necesidades del usuario.
Cómo es la construcción digital antes de la física
El funcionamiento de la impresión 3D en la construcción parte de un modelo digital tridimensional. Una vez definido el diseño, la impresora inicia la fabricación capa por capa, con una precisión milimétrica. El material más utilizado es el hormigón especial para impresión, aunque existen opciones como plásticos reforzados y biocompuestos.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta tecnología presenta ventajas porque permite crear formas complejas y personalizadas, imposibles de lograr con métodos tradicionales; además, la utilización exacta de materiales reduce el impacto ambiental. En algunos casos, incluso se emplean materiales reciclables, incrementando la sostenibilidad de los proyectos.
La inteligencia artificial, por su parte, supervisa continuamente la obra. Analiza en tiempo real el estado de la estructura y ajusta automáticamente parámetros de impresión si detecta desviaciones. También coordina otros sistemas de obra, como drones para inspección y realidad aumentada para visualizar el resultado final antes de la entrega.
PUBLICIDAD
Tipos de viviendas y ejemplos de proyectos
La impresión 3D ha permitido construir desde viviendas unifamiliares personalizadas hasta complejos residenciales. Un ejemplo destacado es una casa en los Países Bajos, levantada en cinco días, que demuestra la eficiencia térmica y la resistencia estructural de este tipo de construcciones.
El grado de personalización es otro rasgo distintivo. La tecnología permite adaptar cada casa a las necesidades y preferencias de los propietarios, tanto en distribución como en acabados y detalles arquitectónicos.
PUBLICIDAD
Los arquitectos pueden diseñar soluciones a medida, integrando sistemas inteligentes para controlar iluminación, climatización y seguridad.
Ventajas y desafíos de la construcción con impresión 3D e IA
La reducción de costes es una de las principales ventajas de este método. Al emplear únicamente la cantidad necesaria de material y automatizar gran parte del proceso, los gastos asociados a mano de obra y recursos disminuyen considerablemente. Además, el control digital permite cumplir plazos ajustados sin sacrificar calidad.
PUBLICIDAD
El proceso también destaca por su flexibilidad de diseño. La impresión 3D posibilita la creación de estructuras complejas, curvas y formas orgánicas, que antes requerían técnicas costosas o eran directamente inviables. Los arquitectos pueden experimentar con nuevas geometrías y materiales, abriendo un abanico de posibilidades para la vivienda personalizada.
No obstante, existen desafíos aún por resolver. La falta de normativas claras para la impresión 3D en construcción limita su adopción masiva. Además, la inversión inicial en impresoras de gran escala y la capacitación del personal representan obstáculos para pequeñas empresas.

articles.title: L’IA consomme-t-elle trop d’électricité ? L'Arcep veut faire le point
articles.text:
Depuis 2020, l’Arcep réclame chaque année aux acteurs du numérique français leurs chiffres environnementaux : électricité consommée, émissions de gaz à effet de serre, volumes d’eau prélevés. Le périmètre s’est élargi au fil des éditions, des opérateurs télécoms aux équipementiers mobiles, puis aux fabricants de câbles en fibre optique lors de la dernière livraison en mai. L’autorité vise désormais un cran au-dessus.
Une consultation ouverte, une collecte prévue pour 2027
L’Arcep a mis en consultation publique un projet de décision destiné à intégrer les fournisseurs de services d’IA générative à son enquête annuelle. Le calendrier demande un peu de patience : la campagne de collecte concernée est celle de 2027, pour une publication en 2028.
L’autorité mène par ailleurs depuis le début de l’année des échanges avec ces fournisseurs et avec les exploitants de centres de données, afin de définir des indicateurs qui tiennent méthodologiquement la route (exercice moins évident qu’il n’y paraît, puisqu’il faut isoler ce qui relève de l’IA dans une infrastructure qui héberge aussi tout le reste).
À lire aussi : Data centers – une loi va faciliter leur installation, les associations s’inquiètent
L’idée générale rappelle celle de l’étiquette énergie collée sur les lave-linges : rendre comparable ce qui ne l’est pas, en imposant les mêmes cases à remplir à tout le monde. Le régulateur n’entend pas fixer de plafond ni sanctionner une consommation, seulement obtenir des chiffres qu’il puisse publier.
Les centres de données grossissent plus vite que le reste
La dernière enquête donne la mesure du problème avec les données 2024 : la consommation électrique des exploitants de centres de données progresse de 12 % en un an. Leurs émissions de gaz à effet de serre bondissent quant à elles de 23 % sur la même période, l’électricité utilisée étant devenue plus carbonée. L’usage suit la même pente puisque 48 % des Français déclaraient utiliser l’IA générative en 2025, soit 28 points de plus en deux ans, avec une pointe à 85 % chez les 18-24 ans.
Reste le motif réel de l’opération, que l’autorité a formulé sans détour dans un rapport publié au printemps. Les concepteurs de modèles et les fournisseurs de services communiquent trop peu sur leurs impacts environnementaux réels, ce qui rend toute comparaison sérieuse impossible. Les utilisateurs se retrouvent donc privés des éléments qui leur permettraient de choisir en connaissance de cause. Autrement dit, les chiffres qui circulent aujourd’hui viennent essentiellement de ceux qui ont intérêt à les présenter sous leur meilleur jour.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra vs Oppo Find N6 hinge comparison — there's still a clear winner
articles.text:
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's Flex Titanium display is impressive, but another phone is still the creaseless king
Close, but no cigar
Samsung’s latest foldables have arrived with much fanfare. There’s the uniquely proportioned Galaxy Z Fold 8, which looks to be the precursor to the foldable iPhone Ultra later this year; the more conventional-looking Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra; and Samsung’s thinnest and lightest flip phone ever in the Galaxy Z Flip 8.
The first two of those three phones boast Samsung's new Flex Titanium display technology, which gives them thinner, flatter, and more robust displays than any Galaxy foldables before them. And having spent time with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra already, I’ve been impressed with the progress Samsung has made in reducing the appearance of the crease, specifically.
From front-on, you can hardly make out the crease at all, and at an angle, it’s less obvious than on the Galaxy Z Fold 7. Running my finger across the middle of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's display, there’s only a very subtle undulation running down the center. It’s so subtle that I’d wager you’ll stop registering that it's even there after spending a few weeks with the new phone.
And yet, for how impressed I am with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s display, I know there’s already something better available.
Enter the contender
The Oppo Find N6 launched in March 2026, four months earlier than Samsung’s Z8 series, and the big selling point was the claim that Oppo had managed to remove the crease in the foldable screen entirely.
Now, while that isn’t strictly true — at some acute angles, you can still see the crease — what is pretty amazing is the fact you can run your finger across the entire 8.12-inch display and not feel any interruption on the part of the screen that bends when folded.
I’ve been fortunate enough to have used most foldables, including reviewing the original Galaxy Fold, and the screen crease has always been there.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Most of the time, when you’re looking straight-on at the screen, it does disappear as your eyes focus on the content, but have the light hit at a certain angle, or run your finger across, and you’re immediately reminded of the minor imperfection.
I was stunned when I first got my hands on the Oppo Find N6. Swiping my finger back and forth across the middle of the display and feeling nothing, I thought, 'This is the next frontier of foldables.'
To make sure I wasn’t just looking at the Oppo through rose-tinted specs, I took it to the Samsung preview event so I could experience it side-by-side with the Z Fold 8 Ultra. And sure enough, the Oppo continued to impress with a screen that is smoother and flatter than Samsung’s, but not by much.
Which one is right for you?
Make no mistake, these are two very accomplished, flagship foldables. Both have similarly sized exterior and interior screens, and both are powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset.
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is thinner, lighter, and actually readily available in multiple markets. It also has a brighter display (a peak brightness of 3,000 nits vs 2,500 nits on the Oppo) and the firm’s Galaxy AI, Now Brief, and Now Nudge features on top of Google’s Gemini assistant.
The Oppo Find N6 has the smoothest, flattest foldable display, an edge in the camera hardware, a bigger battery and faster charging — yet its availability is limited to just a few Asian markets at the time of writing.
So, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra wins by default, which doesn’t feel particularly satisfying as a conclusion, but this shouldn’t diminish the progress that’s been made.
The main issue with foldable displays has been conquered. The next major hurdle we need manufacturers to clear is price.
The Z Fold 8 Ultra is available for pre-order for a lofty $2,099.99 / £1,899 / AU$2,999, which makes it Samsung’s most expensive foldable ever (if we ignore the limited-run TriFold). The Z Fold 8 (from $1,899.99 / £1,699 / AU$2,699) and Z Flip 8 (from $1,199.99 / £1,149 / AU$1,949) are cheaper, but they’re still not cheap.
So, if a manufacturer can find a way to deliver the same premium features for under $1,200/ £1,200 / AU$1,500, it could open the foldable floodgates.

articles.title: Disgruntled gamer builds booby-trapped Steam Deck with 3D-printed spikes and a built-in taser — Raspberry Pi powers speaker, camera, and alarm to stop family members draining his battery
articles.text:
Disgruntled gamer builds booby-trapped Steam Deck with 3D-printed spikes and a built-in taser — Raspberry Pi powers speaker, camera, and alarm to stop family members draining his battery
Sometimes you just don’t want to share your precious devices.
A Steam Deck devotee was so fed up with their family borrowing their handheld and leaving it with a flat battery that they have resorted to quite extreme measures. On the Steam Deck subreddit, ConroyyJenkinss says that they have modded the console with a range of anti-sharing measures, including a 3D-modeled spiky case and a taser, among other things.
In the video embedded above, you can see ConroyyJenkinss augmented Steam Deck, which has basically sacrificed the Steam Deck’s comfy ergonomics on the altar of defensive design. Its hand-filling gentle curves have been nullified with a 3D-printed case that was modeled by the anti-sharing Steam Deck owner in Blender. We hope this Steam Deck chastity belt is easily detachable by the owner for when ConroyyJenkinss wants to have some fun.
The hostile architecture-inspired case has another scary trick or two up its sleeve, though. “To make it worse, I rigged up a Raspberry Pi with a small speaker, an object detection camera, and a servo motor,” the Redditor explains. “[I] wrote a py script so if the camera sees someone in frame, it plays a goofy audio clip, waits a few seconds and then the servo triggers a taser to scare them away.” So at least those tempted to touch this spiky handheld get warned before potentially being tased.
Most importantly, ConroyyJenkinss asserts that their Steam Deck anti-sharing measures have done the job. “Nobody touches my Steam Deck anymore,” concludes the dangerous DIYer. Answering some queries in the Reddit thread, the embattled Steam Deck owner admits having to remove the case and disarm the taser to use their own handheld is “a hassle but overall worth it.” Now other family members ask permission to have a gaming session on the portable console.
In recent weeks, Steam Decks have joined the ranks of the desirable devices that have been heavily impacted by the RAMpocalypse. It’s nice to share things, but we fully understand ConroyyJenkinss protecting his precious unit, especially against the devil-may-care battery drainers in the family.

articles.title: 7 Books that help you become less reactive and more reflective
articles.text:
7 Books that help you become less reactive & more reflective
Discover seven insightful books that help you develop emotional control, self-awareness, patience, and a more reflective mindset.
In a world of constant notifications, instant opinions, and endless distractions, reacting has become easier than reflecting. We respond to criticism before understanding it, make decisions based on emotions, and allow temporary frustrations to influence long-term choices.
Yet some of the wisest thinkers throughout history have argued that the quality of our lives depends largely on the space between an event and our response to it. The ability to pause, think, and act intentionally is a skill that can be cultivated. Books can be powerful teachers in this process. They encourage us to slow down, examine our thoughts, and develop greater emotional awareness.
7 Valuable lessons on becoming reflective in everyday life
1. Meditations by Marcus Aurelius
Written as personal reflections rather than a formal book, Meditations remains one of the most influential works on self-control and inner calm. Marcus Aurelius repeatedly reminds himself that external events are often beyond his control, but his response to them is not.
Instead of reacting with anger, frustration, or resentment, he advocates examining situations rationally and focusing on what truly matters. The book teaches readers to create distance between emotions and actions, making it a timeless guide for developing patience and perspective.
2. The Untethered Soul by Michael A. Singer
Many reactions begin with thoughts we barely notice. The Untethered Soul encourages readers to observe those thoughts instead of immediately identifying with them. Michael Singer explores the concept of the inner voice and how much of our emotional suffering comes from becoming trapped in mental narratives.
By learning to witness thoughts rather than automatically believe them, readers develop greater emotional freedom. The book offers a practical framework for cultivating awareness and responding to life with more clarity and less impulsiveness.
3. Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman
Nobel Prize-winning psychologist Daniel Kahneman explains how the human mind operates through two systems of thinking: one fast, intuitive, and emotional, and the other slower, deliberate, and analytical. Much of our reactivity comes from relying too heavily on fast thinking.
The book reveals the cognitive biases and mental shortcuts that influence decisions without our awareness. By understanding how the mind works, readers become better equipped to pause, question assumptions, and make more thoughtful choices.
4. The Daily Stoic by Ryan Holiday and Stephen Hanselman
Drawing from Stoic philosophy, The Daily Stoic offers short reflections designed to encourage calmness, resilience, and self-awareness. Each entry reminds readers to focus on what they can control and release what they cannot.
Over time, this practice helps reduce emotional reactivity and develop a more measured approach to challenges. The book's daily format makes reflection a habit rather than an occasional exercise.
5. The Things You Can See Only When You Slow Down by Haemin Sunim
Modern life often encourages speed, but wisdom frequently requires slowing down. In this thoughtful book, Haemin Sunim explores mindfulness, compassion, relationships, and emotional balance. He suggests that many problems become clearer when we stop rushing through life and give ourselves time to observe our experiences.
The book encourages readers to respond with understanding rather than react out of habit or emotion. Its gentle insights make it particularly valuable for those seeking greater calm in daily life.
6. Emotional Agility by Susan David
Psychologist Susan David argues that emotional health is not about suppressing difficult feelings but learning how to engage with them wisely. Emotional Agility teaches readers to recognise emotions without allowing them to dictate behaviour.
Instead of reacting automatically, individuals learn to examine what their emotions are communicating and choose responses aligned with their values. The book provides practical tools for navigating stress, uncertainty, and interpersonal challenges with greater awareness and flexibility.
7. Man's Search for Meaning by Viktor E. Frankl
Few books illustrate the power of thoughtful response more profoundly than Frankl's classic work. Reflecting on his experiences in Nazi concentration camps, Frankl observed that while people cannot always control their circumstances, they can choose how they respond to them.
His famous insight, that there is a space between stimulus and response, captures the essence of reflection. Within that space lies the freedom to choose actions based on values rather than immediate emotions. The lesson remains as relevant today as ever.
Looking beyond the pages
Reflection is a skill that requires patience and practice. In a culture that rewards speed and immediate reactions, choosing to pause and think can feel countercultural. Yet it is often the difference between regret and wisdom. These books offer valuable guidance for anyone seeking a more thoughtful way of living, because growth often begins not when we react faster, but when we learn to pause long enough to respond wisely.

articles.title: Plus de 4000 URL à supprimer : la police européenne s'attaque à nouveau aux pirates sans scrupule de « The Com »
articles.text:
« The Com », un réseau extrémiste décentralisé qui recrute et manipule des mineurs en ligne, vient de se retrouver dans le viseur des forces de l’ordre. Entre juin et juillet 2026, des enquêteurs venus de Belgique, de Finlande, de Hongrie, d’Irlande, du Luxembourg, des Pays-Bas, du Portugal, d’Espagne et de Suède ont mené des « Referral Action Days », des journées d’action consacrées au signalement des contenus en ligne liés au réseau criminel.
À lire aussi : Fuites de données – la France devient la victime numéro un d’Europe, c’est de pire en pire
Passer au crible Internet
Lors de ces journées d’action, organisées depuis 2015, des enquêteurs spécialisés venus de plusieurs pays d’Europe se regroupent, généralement pendant un ou deux jours, pour passer au crible Internet et identifier des contenus problématiques sur les plateformes en ligne.
Chapeautée par Europol, l’initiative a permis de perturber l’écosystème numérique de The Com. Au cours de l’opération, 4 340 adresses web ont été signalées par les enquêteurs aux plateformes numériques. Ces adresses URL doivent désormais être retirées dans les plus brefs délais. Les contenus visés incluent des vidéos d’agressions violentes, des scènes de cruauté envers les animaux, ainsi que des manuels expliquant comment fabriquer des explosifs artisanaux.
À lire aussi : Une fuite de données « sans précédent » frappe des milliers de diplomates dans le monde
Des criminels sans le moindre scrupule
Comme l’explique Europol dans son communiqué, The Com est composé d’une myriade de groupuscules, surtout d’extrême droite, qui recrutent et manipulent leurs victimes via les réseaux sociaux, les applications de messagerie et les plateformes de jeu vidéo. Ces groupes cherchent surtout à séduire les mineurs. Une fois que c’est fait, ils vont tenter de les pousser, bien souvent par l’extorsion, vers l’automutilation, la violence ou la production de contenus pédopornographiques.
Europol distingue plusieurs sous-groupes au sein de ce réseau. « Offline Com » prône les dégradations et le terrorisme, tandis que « Cyber Com » se spécialise dans les intrusions informatiques et les ransomwares. Le sous-groupe « (S)extortion Com » pousse quant à lui des mineurs vers des actes sexuels et l’automutilation. Enfin, « 764 », apparu en 2021, incite des jeunes internautes fragiles à produire du contenu explicite, qui eest ensuite utilisé à des fins de chantage. Par ailleurs, The Com a été relié à plusieurs cyberattaques d’envergure, dont le piratage du casino MGM à Las Vegas, survenu en 2023, ainsi que les attaques par ransomware contre plusieurs entreprises britanniques l’an dernier.
Pour rappel, The Com s’est déjà retrouvé dans le collimateur d’Europol cette année. En mars dernier, les autorités ont interpellé 30 criminels accusés de faire partie du réseau extrémiste. Dans la foulée, près de 200 autres truands avaient été identifiés.

articles.title: "¿De verdad está pasando esto?": Ryan Gosling cumple su sueño y sustituye a Nicolas Cage en el papel de este superhéroe de Marvel
articles.text:
Ryan Gosling lo deseaba y Marvel lo ha hecho realidad. Tras insistir durante años en que le encantaría interpretar a Ghost Rider (el Motorista Fantasma), el deseo del actor de 'Barbie' finalmente se ha cumplido. Durante la Comic-Con de San Diego, Kevin Feige ha anunciado oficialmente que Ryan Gosling dará vida al célebre motorista demoníaco de Marvel en una nueva película.
Gosling fue invitado a subir al escenario del Hall H, donde, emocionado, dijo "¿De verdad está pasando esto? Es un personaje que llevo soñando con interpretar desde hace muchísimo tiempo". Acto seguido, agregó que "solo un director podía hacer esta película", justo antes de dar paso a Shawn Levy, el director de 'Deadpool y Lobezno'.
Una alianza que viene de lejos
Esta no será la primera vez que Shawn Levy dirija a Ryan Gosling. Ambos ya están trabajando juntos en 'Star Wars: Starfighter', cuyo estreno en cines está previsto para el 27 de mayo del año que viene. Después se volverán a encontrar en 'Ghost Rider', cuyo guion quedará en manos de Jonathan Tropper ('The Adam Project', 'The Wrecking Crew'). La fecha de estreno no está confirmada, pero cabe esperar que se vaya al 2028.
De esta manera, Ryan Gosling el relevo de Nicolas Cage en el papel de Johnny Blaze. Cage interpretó al personaje en 'Ghost Rider: El motorista fantasma' en el año 2007, así como en la secuela 'Ghost Rider: Espíritu de venganza' en el año 2012.
Ambas películas fueron absolutamente destrozadas por la crítica, aunque fueron sorprendentemente rentables. La primera, cuyo presupuesto fue de 110 millones de dólares, tiene un 26% en Rotten Tomatoes, pero recaudó 228,7 millones de dólares. La segunda, a pesar de ser aún peor (un 18%), recaudó 132,5 millones. No generó pérdidas directas, pero sí fue un indicador suficiente para que Sony decidiera vender los derechos del personaje, que acabaron volviendo a Marvel Studios.
Según expuso Kevin Feige en 2013, "cuando un personaje vuelve a nosotros suele ser porque los otros estudios ya no quieren hacer más películas, lo que casi siempre significa que las entregas anteriores no fueron especialmente bien recibidas. Todos tienen potencial, pero no vamos a decir '¡Lo tenemos de vuelta, hagámoslo ya!".
13 años más tarde, tras su paso por la cuarta temporada de 'Agents of SHIELD' y con el cine de superhéroes en horas bajas, parece que sí es el momento. En lo que respecta a Ryan Gosling, el actor se prepara para un futuro dorado en el cine comercial tras los éxitos consecutivos de 'Barbie' y 'El especialista'. El siguiente paso lo dará ya dentro de Disney y en la franquicia Star Wars, otra saga que tampoco pasa por su mejor momento.

articles.title: Apple aurait enfin trouvé la solution à l’un des grands défauts de l’iPad
articles.text:
Après des années d’attente et de réclamations, Apple aurait enfin mis au point un iPad mini résistant à l’eau. Son lancement serait prévu cet automne, plus précisément en octobre. Si un tel produit venait à se confirmer, il serait possible de l’utiliser dans des environnements humides ou encore aux abords d’une piscine l’été prochain. En revanche, il faudra très probablement éviter de l’immerger dans de l’eau salée ou chlorée.
Enfin un iPad mini résistant à l’humidité
Alors que certaines tablettes de ses concurrents offrent une certification IP68 depuis maintenant un moment, l’iPad mini doit toujours être tenu éloigné des points d’eau. C’est bien simple, les différentes tablettes d’Apple n’ont jamais bénéficié de certification IP. Du moins, pour l’instant. En effet, selon les informations de Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple prévoirait de lancer le premier iPad mini équipé d’un écran OLED, mais aussi résistant à l’humidité, en octobre prochain.
Pour l’entreprise à la pomme, le défi consiste à supprimer les ouvertures du châssis par lesquelles l’eau et la poussière peuvent s’infiltrer. Pour y parvenir, Apple aurait mis au point un système de haut-parleurs à vibration qui émet le son à travers des surfaces planes de la tablette. Certaines parties du boîtier pourraient ainsi faire office de diaphragme acoustique, supprimant l’une des principales voies d’infiltration tout en renforçant l’étanchéité de l’appareil. Pour l’instant, nous ne savons pas quel serait l’indice de protection IP de l’iPad mini.
Dans tous les cas, cela ne signifie pas qu’il sera possible d’immerger l’appareil sans précaution. Si un tel produit voit bel et bien le jour, il faudra probablement éviter tout contact prolongé avec l’eau salée ou l’eau chlorée d’une piscine. En revanche, l’appareil devrait être capable de résister aux éclaboussures, comme dans une salle de bain ou au bord d’une piscine. Pour rappel, l’iPhone 17 présente une certification IP68 : il est résistant à la poussière et est censé supporter une immersion dans l’eau douce jusqu’à 6 mètres pendant 30 minutes.
Apple travaille sur la confection d’un iPad étanche depuis maintenant des années
En 2014, Apple a déposé un brevet décrit comme un « système acoustique à panneaux actionnés mécaniquement » permettant de produire du son en faisant vibrer des surfaces planes du châssis, supprimant ainsi la nécessité d’utiliser des grilles de haut-parleurs traditionnelles. En 2025, soit plus de dix ans plus tard, Mark Gurman rapportait qu’Apple travaillait toujours activement sur un système de résistance à l’eau pour l’iPad, comparable à celui des iPhone. Après des années d’attente, il semble donc que l’année 2026 soit la bonne : il sera enfin possible d’utiliser un iPad mini à proximité de zones humides. Reste maintenant à voir quel sera le prix du nouvel iPad mini.

articles.title: Renault rafle la mise avec les voitures électriques, à la deuxième place des meilleurs vendeurs européens
articles.text:
Renault rafle la mise avec les voitures électriques, à la deuxième place des meilleurs vendeurs européens
L’année 2026 réussit à Renault, avec une seconde place au classement des ventes de voitures électriques en Europe. Une transition réussie qui promet de s’intensifier avec la nouvelle petite Twingo E-Tech.
Alors que Tesla domine clairement le marché européen avec ses Model Y et Model 3, Renault n’a pas dit son dernier mot sur le marché des voitures électriques. Pour le 1er semestre 2026, la marque prend la 2e place des ventes sur le Vieux Continent. Portée par le succès immédiat de la célèbre R5 E-Tech, cette offensive confirme la puissance du groupe automobile tricolore, qui a maintenant une gamme électrifiée de plus en plus complète pour séduire.
Comment Renault bouscule le marché des voitures électriques en Europe ?
En Europe, Renault annonce tout d’abord dans son communiqué que 66,3 % (+7,2 points par rapport à la même période en 2025) de ses véhicules vendus au 1er semestre 2026 étaient désormais électrifiés. Les modèles 100 % électriques bondissent quant à eux, représentant plus d'un quart des ventes (26,6 %) de la marque aujourd’hui, contre 16,3 % précédemment.
Une performance qui s'appuie largement sur la popularité de la Renault 5 E-Tech, “véhicule électrique le plus vendu du segment B en Europe, tandis que Renault 4 E-Tech electric s'impose comme la référence du segment B-SUV électrique auprès des particuliers”. La nouvelle citadine compacte Twingo E-Tech commence de son côté à faire son petit effet auprès des Français, pendant que le Scenic E-Tech séduit de plus en plus de familles à la recherche d'un modèle spacieux.
Du côté des marques dérivées, Renault connaît un succès marqué avec Alpine qui grimpe à 80 % d’immatriculations en tout électrique, notamment grâce à l’Alpine A290 et au lancement de l’A390. Dacia voit de son côté les ventes d’hybrides s’envoler, portées par l'engouement autour des nouveaux Duster et Bigster, permettant à cette motorisation de représenter désormais une vente sur quatre (+30,2 %). La marque Renault se hisse d’ailleurs désormais à la seconde place des ventes sur le marché hybride européen.
Si l'Europe reste le fer de lance de cette offensive verte, le groupe maintient un cap solide à l'échelle mondiale. Au cours de ce premier semestre 2026, les ventes globales se stabilisent à plus d'1,16 million d'unités vendues à travers le monde (légère baisse de 0,4 % par rapport au 1er semestre 2025). Hors d’Europe, le constructeur français connaît quand même une croissance de +2,8 %, avec des hausses prononcées en Inde (+61,2 %), en Turquie (+15,4 %), au Maroc (+13,7 %) ainsi qu'au Brésil (+5,3 %).
De quoi aborder le second semestre 2026 en toute sérénité, avec au passage deux lancements attendus : le Trafic Van E-Tech et le pick-up Niagara (exclusif à l’Amérique latine), mais aussi les Dacia Sandero hybride, la nouvelle Dacia Spring, le Dacia Striker et l'Alpine A390 en version GTS.
